label: D2: rare transition a2 -> S1 (state S1 shown after choosing a2), early-to-mid episode
explanation: Fires only at D2 (never D1/GO), when the observed state is S1 and the last-action input is a2, i.e. the a2->S1 rare transition; all variables are observed at D2. 98% of activation mass lies on a2->S1 D2 steps; a weak residue (~1.6% of mass, activations <0.35) is on a1->S1 common steps. It never fires on S2 (55 steps) or on rewarded inputs. Strong episode-time dependence: rate falls after trial ~60 and is ~0 from trial 70 on, so the ep_trial<70 term raises precision from 0.57 to 0.82 at almost no recall cost (the agent can track elapsed time in its hidden state). Magnitude: the largest activations (~0.95-1.0) in examples occur when the previous trial was rewarded (r1 at D1); after unrewarded trials activations are lower (~0.5-0.7), and adding prev_reward==1 gives precision 0.95 but recall 0.69. Remaining false positives are mostly a2->S1 steps after an unrewarded previous trial with a2 previous choice uncommon.

issues: The factual claims hold on the dev profile. Activity is D2 only: D1 and GO have 0 active steps. 100% of activation mass is on in_state==1, and only 55 active steps are on S2. in_rew==1 is never active. in_action==2 carries 98.4% of mass, and the a1 remainder is 1.6%. The activity rate by ep_trial falls from 0.048 to 0.025 at trials 60-69, to 0.002 at 70-79, and to 0 from 80 on.
Test scores reproduce exactly: P 0.805, R 0.931, F1 0.863, mass recall 0.980. Without ep_trial<70 the test scores are P 0.554, F1 0.697, so the time cut is doing real work.

The remaining false positives are systematic but already disclosed: a2->S1 D2 steps after an unrewarded previous trial. The predicate restricted to prev_reward==0 has precision 0.56, and restricted to prev_reward==1 it has P 0.946 / R 0.691 / mass recall 0.804. Since recall is 0.69 but mass recall is 0.80, the rewarded cases carry more activation per step, which numerically backs the magnitude claim the explanation made only from example windows. Splitting by the hidden good state also leaves a gap: good==2 has P 0.87, good==1 has P 0.61.

The ep_trial<70 cutoff may stand in for the model's value-head output, because value falls over the episode. The predicate base & (value>=7.0) & (value<7.6) gets test F1 0.864, P 0.878, R 0.851, about the same as the ep_trial version. Combining both (ep_trial<70 & value<7.6) gets F1 0.867. The explanation could mention that the time dependence might really be a value or reward-expectation dependence, but this does not refute the label.
The missed activations (2.0% of mass) are weak a1->S1 common activations and other scattered cases. I found no systematic missed class.
